Unit 1 of 10: Completing the Square and the Vertex

Key ideas

  • Completed square form: ax² + bx + c = a(x + p)² + q.
  • Method: factor out a from the x terms, halve the coefficient of x inside the bracket, then correct the constant.
  • The vertex of y = a(x + p)² + q is at (−p, q). If a > 0 it is a minimum; if a < 0 it is a maximum.
  • Uses: the vertex, the range of a quadratic function, showing an expression is always positive, and finding inverses.

Worked examples

Example 1: express 2x² − 12x + 5 in the form a(x + b)² + c.

  • 2(x² − 6x) + 5 = 2[(x − 3)² − 9] + 5 = 2(x − 3)² − 13.
  • The vertex is (3, −13), a minimum, so the least value is −13.

Example 2: show that x² + 6x + 14 > 0 for all x.

  • x² + 6x + 14 = (x + 3)² + 5. Since (x + 3)² ≥ 0, the expression is at least 5, so it is always positive.

Example 3: find the maximum value of 7 + 4x − x².

  • −(x² − 4x) + 7 = −[(x − 2)² − 4] + 7 = 11 − (x − 2)². Maximum 11 at x = 2.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) Express 3x² + 12x + 1 in the form a(x + b)² + c. [3]

(b) State the coordinates of the vertex of y = 3x² + 12x + 1 and whether it is a maximum or minimum. [2]

(c) Hence find the range of f(x) = 3x² + 12x + 1 for x ∈ ℝ. [1]

(d) Express 5 − 8x − 2x² in the form p − q(x + r)² and state its greatest value. [4]

Answers and mark guide:

  • (a) 3(x² + 4x) + 1 = 3[(x + 2)² − 4] + 1 = 3(x + 2)² − 11 (B1 for a = 3, M1 for completing the square, A1).
  • (b) (−2, −11) (B1), minimum (B1).
  • (c) f(x) ≥ −11 (B1).
  • (d) −2(x² + 4x) + 5 = −2[(x + 2)² − 4] + 5 = 13 − 2(x + 2)² (M1 A1 A1); greatest value 13 (B1).

Common mistakes

  1. Forgetting to multiply the "−(b/2)²" correction by a.
  2. Wrong sign of the vertex x-coordinate: (x − 3)² gives x = 3.
  3. Treating a negative a as a minimum.
  4. Writing the range with x instead of f(x).
  5. Dropping the constant term.

Quick recall

  1. Vertex of y = (x + 4)² − 7?
  2. Is y = −2(x − 1)² + 3 a maximum or minimum?
  3. Complete the square: x² − 10x.
  4. Least value of (x − 5)² + 2?
  5. Why is (x + a)² ≥ 0?

Answers: 1) (−4, −7). 2) A maximum, at (1, 3). 3) (x − 5)² − 25. 4) 2. 5) A square of a real number is never negative.
